faqs.a: Entropy in bits = length x log2(character set size). A 12-character password using all 94 printable characters has about 78.7 bits. Every extra bit doubles the guesses needed.
Mostly length. A 16-character lowercase-only password (75 bits) beats an 8-character mixed one (52 bits) and is easier to type. The best password is long and unique.
faqs.q: Is length or complexity more important?

faqs.a: A random 8-character password has about 52 bits: crackable in hours on fast hardware. It survives only against slow online guessing with lockouts. Never reuse it anywhere important.
No. Entropy math assumes random characters. 'Password123!' looks complex but falls to dictionary attacks in seconds. Use random or passphrase-style passwords instead.

It is a rough order-of-magnitude estimate assuming 10 billion guesses per second (fast offline hardware). Real attacks vary hugely: slow salted hashes resist far longer, leaked unsalted hashes far less.
faqs.q: How accurate is the crack-time estimate?

faqs.a: The strongest practical option: a long random string from a password manager, unique per site, plus two-factor authentication. Passphrases of 5+ random words are a good memorable alternative.

password-strength-checker.formula:
Entropy (bits) = Length x log2(Charset size)

Charset sizes: lowercase 26, uppercase 26, digits 10, symbols 32.
Mixed example: 26 + 26 + 10 + 32 = 94.

Crack time = 2^bits / guesses-per-second (assumes 10 billion/sec).

Example: "Tr7!kq#9xZm" = 10 chars x log2(94) = 10 x 6.55 = 65.5 bits -> Good.

keyFacts: Password strength = entropy: how many guesses an attacker needs on average.
Entropy = length x log2(character set size).
Each extra bit doubles the work for the attacker.
Tiers here: under 40 bits very weak, 40-60 weak, 60-80 good, 80-100 strong, 100+ excellent.
A 12-character all-type password has about 78.7 bits.

password-strength-checker.workedExample:
Password: "Tr7!kq#9xZm" (10 characters).
1. Character types: lowercase, uppercase, digits, symbols all present.
2. Charset = 26 + 26 + 10 + 32 = 94.
3. Entropy = 10 x log2(94) = 10 x 6.55 = 65.5 bits.
4. Tier: 60-80 bits = Good.
5. Crack time: 2^65.5 / 10^10 seconds = about 171 years.

Compare: an 8-character lowercase-only password has 8 x 4.7 = 37.6 bits (Very weak).
